answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay: every agent must lock a small refundable bond before it can transact, and its trust score grows only through repeated, verified work over time, like water slowly carving a canyon. New identities start near zero, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets buys no influence; the bond makes each fake costly, while the slow reputation curve is the velvet rope that keeps an oasis of honest agents from being flooded by cheap copies.
